issues.legal_issue: A court hearing an appeal must give effect to a proved, lawful compromise that settles the appeal.
material_facts: The parties entered into a written compromise settling their pending disputes, including the dispute in the appeal, and providing that the respondent would withdraw the appeal.
The respondent refused to withdraw the appeal, and the appellant asked the appellate court to dispose of it in accordance with the compromise.
The fact and validity of the compromise were not disputed.
issues.conclusion: The appellate court was bound to accept the compromise and dismiss the appeal in accordance with its terms; the High Court erred in setting aside that dismissal.
issues.legal_principle: Order 23 Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires the court, when satisfied that a suit has been settled wholly or in part by a lawful agreement, to record the compromise and pass a decree in accordance with it so far as it relates to the suit. For this purpose, “suit” includes an appeal. The provision is mandatory. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.appeal_proceeding: The matter before the court is an appeal.
predicates.lawful_compromise_covers_appeal: The parties made a lawful compromise that settles the dispute in the appeal.
predicates.compromise_proved: The compromise was proved to the court's satisfaction.

issues.definition: When a proved lawful compromise settles a dispute in an appeal, the appeal must be disposed of in accordance with that compromise.
